A GlitchTip user says it works well but is a bit hard to deploy because of its many moving parts, which they blame on F/OSS Sentry. They like being able to use the Sentry reporting ecosystem with it, including newer reporters such as Svelte.

Comparison with self-hosted Sentry: GlitchTip seems to need only 4 components (backend, workers, Redis, PostgreSQL). Self-hosted Sentry needs at least a dozen, including ClickHouse, ZooKeeper, Kafka, Redis and multiple backends. The commenter says self-hosted Sentry is stable once deployed but 'a lot to deal with.'

A user running GlitchTip at very small scale says stability has been great and they haven't had to babysit it. They note Django/Rails projects take a bit more to deploy than ideal; they would prefer a single binary/container plus a database, and Django isn't that by default.

A happy GlitchTip user of about a year finds it super easy to self-host. Because it uses the existing Sentry libs, they find it really reliable: 'One of the most set and forget services I've had the pleasure of using.' Given the choice, they would take Sentry+GlitchTip over Rollbar for the Sentry libs alone.

A user noticed uBlock blocking browser error reporting on the hosted product. A custom subdomain using the relay container, and a sub-path on the primary domain, were both still blocked. They call this an Achilles heel for front-end error reporting, given that roughly 40% of users may run ad-blockers.

When the stable release launched, a visitor found that clicking any blog post on the GlitchTip site led to the installation guide. They also couldn't find a feature overview or screenshots, which they wanted to see when browsing a project site.
